name: Centrism
summary: Centrism is a position between left and right that favours moderate, gradual and pragmatic reform. Its best-documented strands are Third Way and radical centrism, which accept market economies while keeping a liberal welfare state, and stress opportunity with responsibility. It has no fixed program, so many policy answers are inferences.
scope: Mainstream Western centrism as documented in Third Way politics (Giddens, Blair, Clinton, Schroeder) and radical centrism (Satin, Halstead and Lind, Avlon). Excludes parties merely labelled centrist, centrist populism and agrarian or Christian-democratic variants. As a positional label rather than a program, many answers are low-confidence inferences.
